rulings.docket_item: P03-012 (cluster c09, span web:Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.6, unit_type saying_cluster): does any correctly-tiered, genuinely discriminating cohesion driver carry the pair as a saying_cluster, or is the revert to two atomic single_saying rows adopted? The peer-upheld remedy was a boundary change in disguise; the phase-1 author re-derived and confirmed its three legs and correctly refused to execute it without adoption.
rulings.decision: BOUNDARY CHANGE ADOPTED -- the row reverts to two atomic single_saying rows. Exact new span set: { "Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.5", "Eccl.10.6-Eccl.10.6" }. No correctly-tiered discriminating driver exists: the two members share 0 word-bound content tokens, the sole named driver (the missing coordinating conjunction) is carried by 18 of the chapter's 20 verse-openers including the excluded neighbour, the 'apposition' reading it rests on is not what the bytes show, and the one real lexical tie in the stretch runs from the row's opening verse to the verse it excludes. The rival three-verse respan over web:Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.7 was considered and is DECLINED on the bytes.
rulings.grounds: Ruled under the B-5-controlling standard set at B-4 (r1): a skeleton-tier driver is admissible, but it must be word-bound, tier-honest, non-thematic and DISCRIMINATING, and where the members' word-bound content-token intersection is empty and no construction run replaces it, no driver has been named at all and the row falls to the sentence zone's single_saying default. Every leg of that test fails here, each re-derived independently at the bytes. (1) FLOOR: the word-bound content-token intersection of oshb:Eccl.10.5 and oshb:Eccl.10.6 is EMPTY -- 0 tokens, function words included -- re-derived from the consonantal skeletons; the same is true of every adjacent pair from web:Eccl.10.3 through web:Eccl.10.9 (0 tokens at 3/4, 4/5, 5/6, 6/7, 7/8, 8/9), which is the true-sentence-literature texture this chapter is known for (catchword-adjacent pairs: 3 of 19 chapter-wide, the lowest in the book). There is no catchword, no repeated phrase and no shared construction to name for this pair specifically. (2) DISCRIMINATION: the row's SOLE named driver -- the absence of a coordinating conjunction opening the second member -- is the chapter's overwhelming norm, not a marker. Re-derived by reading all 20 ch-10 verse-initial tokens: exactly 2 open with a coordinating waw, "וְגַם" (oshb:Eccl.10.3, byte tier) and "וְהַסָּכָ֖ל" (oshb:Eccl.10.14, byte tier); the other 18 open asyndetically, INCLUDING both oshb:Eccl.10.6 ("נִתַּ֣ן הַסֶּ֔כֶל", byte tier) and the very verse the row is held apart from, oshb:Eccl.10.7 ("רָאִ֥יתִי", byte tier). A feature carried by 18 of 20 verses in the chapter cannot separate this row's seams; it fails the discrimination condition exactly as the tov-anaphora and the verse-initial causal particle did in the ch-7 rulings. (3) The grammatical label the driver rests on is also wrong at the bytes: oshb:Eccl.10.6 is a complete two-clause sentence with its own subject and predicate and its own coordinated second clause, "וַעֲשִׁירִ֖ים בַּשֵּׁ֥פֶל יֵשֵֽׁבוּ" (oshb:Eccl.10.6, byte tier), matching “and the rich sit in a low place” (web:Eccl.10.6) -- not a nominal standing in apposition to the unnamed error of the preceding verse, so the 'apposition' on which the whole cluster call rests is not a byte-supported reading. (4) CROSS-SEAM: the one real lexical tie anywhere in this stretch runs from the row's OPENING verse to the verse the row EXCLUDES, crossing the row's own closing seam -- "רָאִ֖יתִי" (oshb:Eccl.10.5) collates ACCENT_STRIPPED against oshb:Eccl.10.7 ("רָאִ֥יתִי"), and it touches oshb:Eccl.10.6 not at all. CONTROLLING COUNT OBJECT AND DIGIT PAIR (the primaries and the peer cited different objects): the tie is at the BARE WORD-BOUND observation form -- sweep: 14 verses book-wide, exactly 2 of them in this chapter, web:Eccl.10.5 and web:Eccl.10.7; the wider family object, which admits the prefixed spellings, is a DIFFERENT object at 18 verses book-wide, and that is the digit the device inventory carries. 14 and 18 are two true digits for two different objects and may not be blended. (5) Undisclosed, and confirming that this verse's own signals mark an OPENING rather than a pair: oshb:Eccl.10.5 carries the book's existential evil-formula opener, "יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי" (oshb:Eccl.10.5, byte tier) -- sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the other two outside this chapter -- and the under-the-sun refrain, "תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ" (oshb:Eccl.10.5, byte tier), which is the ONLY site of that refrain in this chapter (sweep: 27 verses book-wide, 1 in ch 10). Both are confined to the first member and neither extends to the second. RIVAL CONSIDERED AND DECLINED: adopting a three-verse respan over web:Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.7 on the observation-formula tie. It is refused on the bytes -- the driver never touches the middle verse, whose word-bound intersection with BOTH ends is empty (0 tokens with the verse before it and 0 with the verse after it), so there is no chain to carry a three-verse span; the driver's exclusivity is weak (14 verses book-wide -- the book's habitual discourse formula, not a local marker); and at web:Eccl.10.7 the formula stands verse-initially, where it OPENS a fresh observation rather than closing an envelope. Over-merging in the book's lowest-cohesion chapter (catchword-adjacent pairs: 3 of 19) is precisely what the sentence zone's atomic default guards against.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED BOUNDARY CHANGE. P03-012 is RETIRED. EXACT NEW SPAN SET, tiling web:Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.6 with no gap or overlap: { "Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.5", "Eccl.10.6-Eccl.10.6" } -- two atomic rows, unit_type single_saying, parent_collection "M Eccl.1.12-Eccl.12.7" on both, full X-X span form on both, new decision_ids assigned by the author wave in canonical order (chunk_index renumbered at assembly). The phase-1 author's refusal to execute this revert without adoption was CORRECT and is commended; the adoption is made here. REQUIRED CONTENT. Row Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.5: ground the atomic verdict on the unit-opening signals the verse's own bytes carry -- the existential evil-formula opener (sweep: 3 verses book-wide; if either other site is cited as a ref, the one sitting in the crosswalk zone must carry its mandated dual qualifier) and the under-the-sun refrain, which is this chapter's only site (sweep: 27 verses book-wide, 1 in this chapter) -- the refrain the retired row left undisclosed. DISCLOSE the observation-formula tie forward to web:Eccl.10.7 with its tier named (accent-stripped across the pair) and its controlling count object and digit (bare word-bound form: 14 verses book-wide, exactly 2 in this chapter), and argue past it rather than ignoring it: the formula opens a fresh observation at each site, which is why it stands verse-initially at the later verse. Row Eccl.10.6-Eccl.10.6: ground the atomic verdict on the verse being one complete two-clause reversal sentence with its own subject and predicate; it may NOT be described as apposition to the preceding verse, and its conjunction-free opening may NOT be cited as cohesion or boundary evidence -- state instead, once, that the chapter's openers are asyndetic in 18 of 20 verses so the feature carries nothing here. The social-inversion image shared with web:Eccl.10.7 is TEXTURE only in device_notes, with the digit that their word-bound intersection is 0 tokens. COMPANION EDIT, MANDATORY -- P03-013 (web:Eccl.10.7-Eccl.10.7, span unchanged) must be touched: both its boundary_rationale and its strongest_rejected_alternative currently rest on the struck facts, describing the preceding verses as an 'asyndetic apposition' pair and distinguishing themselves from it. Rewrite both to ground the atomic verdict on the token-clean seams the bytes actually give (word-bound intersection 0 tokens with the verse before and 0 with the verse after), and to DISCLOSE -- not rely on -- the observation-formula tie back to web:Eccl.10.5 with the same tier and the same controlling count object and digit. SEAM-PAIR SYMMETRY: the 10:6|10:7 seam disclosure is ONE edit whose substance must read the same from both sides; install the new 10:6 row and the P03-013 rewrite in a single pass. SWEEP, not a spot fix. (a) The absent-conjunction warrant class is systemic in kind though small in scope here: exactly 2 rows in the draft set invoke it (P03-012, retired by this ruling, and P03-013, cured by it), so the sweep closes with this ruling -- but the rule stands for the revision wave: no row may cite the absence of a conjunction, or any verse-initial particle, as cohesion or boundary evidence without first checking that feature's distribution across its own chapter's openers and citing the digit. (b) The observation-formula count-object class is live across 16 rows that invoke that formula: any row attaching a DIGIT to it must name which object it counts -- bare word-bound form, 14 verses book-wide, or family object including prefixed spellings, 18 verses book-wide -- and blended citation is forbidden. VERIFY: exact tiling of web:Eccl.10.5-Eccl.10.6 re-checked against the neighbouring rows; parent seams untouched; the preceding row at web:Eccl.10.4 needs no edit. TEST each replacement warrant must pass (the test that killed the original): re-verify that ch-10 verse-initial waw distribution shows asyndeton is not distinctive (2 of 20), re-verify the 0-token content overlap of web:Eccl.10.5 and web:Eccl.10.6, and re-verify that the observation-formula tie runs from web:Eccl.10.5 to web:Eccl.10.7 and not to web:Eccl.10.6; and no driver may be cited for a span whose members it does not itself bind.
